title: Top-two learned prototype beam for bounded state retrieval
question: Does increasing coarse-routing beam width from one prototype to two preserve the learned cosine retriever with a bounded K=8 shortlist?
hypothesis: H_beam: the poor one-prototype result is partly a coarse-routing recall problem; top-two prototype routing with K=8 should materially increase target retention while remaining selective.

arms.name: exhaustive_cosine
arms.intervention: cosine-score all 64 states with the fixed raw-trained width-16 encoder

arms.name: prototype_beam
arms.intervention: top-two learned continuous prototypes, union of capacity-four buckets, cosine rerank over K<=8 states

endpoints.name: proposal_target_retention
endpoints.role: secondary — hidden target is in top-two prototype bucket union

endpoints.name: actual_end_to_end_success
endpoints.role: secondary — downstream output matches hidden truth

decision_rule.condition: prototype_beam actual target recall >= exhaustive_cosine actual target recall - 0.05 AND prototype_beam actual end-to-end success >= exhaustive_cosine actual end-to-end success - 0.05 AND shortlist size <= 8
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for two-prototype learned continuous routing as a selective state-retrieval mechanism on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic ANN guarantees or broad C5

decision_rule.condition: either actual target recall or actual end-to-end success is >0.05 below exhaustive-cosine reference, or shortlist exceeds K=8
decision_rule.licenses: two-prototype learned continuous routing does not preserve the registered capability boundary

held_constant: same prototype centroids and state bucket assignment as C5-PROTOTYPE-SELECTIVE-001
no retraining or prototype refitting in this experiment
no evaluation address or gold target enters prototype construction
